doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Joining Charlie Barnet's band through Jimmy Lamar
summary: After reading about Barnet's band in Down Beat, Marty got a call for the Strand Theater job.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So anyway, with Charlie Barnet, I’m reading a Down Beat magazine and they’ve got a review of Charlie Barnet’s band in California someplace, he was playing the Palladium or

someplace, and I read the names of the guys in the band, like Barney Kessel and all these different people, guys that I know. And I said to my wife gee I’d like to play with that band you know. And the next day I get a call from a guy named — the next day — I get a call from Jimmy Lamar, a saxophone player. He didn’t go with the band but Charlie had contacted him to get some guys for the Strand Theater in New York, he was going to be there for eight weeks, eight or nine weeks. “Marty?” “Yeah.” “Jimmy Lamar.” “Hey, Jimmy, how are you?” He said, “listen, would you like to work with Charlie Barnet’s band?” I said, “get out of here, give me that again, for real?” He says, “yeah, why?” I said, no it’s too long a story. “Okay you’ve got it. Where is he going?” “Strand Theater.” I said, man, boom, just like that, eight weeks. Now we’re at the Strand, Gene Krupa goes into the Capitol Theater around the corner, with his band, and my brother, and we’re running between theaters like to see each other between shows you know. It was great.
Oh it’s a fabulous life, man, I love it.
